ctci6_1_6.description: Replace each maximal run of equal consecutive letters by that letter followed by its decimal run length, including length one. Return the encoded string only when it is strictly shorter than text; otherwise return text unchanged. Letter case is significant.
constraints: text contains 0..10000 English letters A..Z or a..z.
Counts use ordinary base-ten digits without leading zeroes. Empty text returns an empty string.
This is a run encoding, not a total character-frequency encoding: separate runs remain separate.

examples.explanation: For 'zzzzQQQQQx', the runs are z:4, Q:5, x:1. Their encodings form 'z4Q5x1', length 6 instead of 10, so it is returned. For 'zz', the candidate 'z2' ties length 2, so the original 'zz' is returned.

ctci6_2_4.description: Rearrange a singly linked list so that every node with Value < pivot comes before every node with Value >= pivot. Return the new head. Reuse each original node exactly once and preserve its Value. Either relative order within a partition is allowed; stability is not required. ctci6_2_5.description: Add two nonnegative integers encoded as singly linked lists of decimal digits. Return their sum as newly allocated digit nodes in the same digit order. When mostSignificantFirst is false, the head is the units digit; when true, the head is the highest-place digit. Support both orders, covering the forward-order extension of the exercise. Preserve all input values and links, and do not share result nodes with either input.
constraints: Each input is finite and acyclic with 0..2000 digit nodes, each Value in 0..9. Inputs share no nodes.
An empty input denotes zero. If both inputs are empty, return null. Otherwise return a nonempty representation, including [0] for zero.

ctci6_3_1.description: Implement three independent fixed-capacity integer stacks in one payload array. ThreeStacks(capacity) reserves exactly capacity slots per stack. Push, Pop, Peek, IsEmpty and IsFull take a zero-based stack number 0, 1 or 2. Pop removes and returns that stack's most recently pushed value; Peek returns it without removing it. Stacks cannot borrow another stack's unused slots.
constraints: Examples are [operations,arguments]: the first operation constructs the class; each later operation calls that method on the same object. The output has one entry per operation: null for construction/void, a returned value otherwise, or {"error":"code"} for the documented BankError. The judge continues after a method error, so failure must leave state unchanged. A failing-constructor transcript contains only construction because no instance exists afterward. There are 1..2001 operations; integer values and indices fit signed 32 bits.

Capacity must be 1..256; otherwise throw BankError('capacity'). Check stack number first on every operation: outside 0..2 throws BankError('index'). Push on a full stack throws BankError('full'); Pop or Peek on an empty stack throws BankError('empty').

Keep all stack payloads in one integer array of length 3*capacity. Three counters and other constant-sized metadata are allowed. This is the fixed-partition variant established by the public FixedMultiStack interface.

examples.explanation: With capacity 2, push 8 then 3 onto stack 0 and push 7 onto stack 2. Stack 0 is full and its Peek returns 3; stack 2's Peek returns 7. Popping stack 0 returns 3 and leaves 8 at its top. A push to a full stack fails even if stack 1 is empty, because this variant reserves fixed slots.

GetMin returns the smallest value currently in the stack, including duplicates, without removing it. Keep constant algorithmic work per operation by storing enough information when each value is pushed.

The output has one entry per operation: null for construction/void, a returned value otherwise, or {"error":"code"} for the documented BankError. There are 1..2001 operations; integer values and indices fit signed 32 bits.
MinStack() starts empty. Pop, Peek and GetMin on an empty stack throw BankError('empty'). IsEmpty returns a boolean and never throws.

ctci6_3_3.description: Implement a stack split into smaller stacks of at most capacity values. Push adds to the last small stack, creating one if needed. Pop removes the globally newest value. PopAt(index) removes the top of the selected zero-based small stack, then rolls over the bottom value of each following stack to fill the preceding gap. Remove an empty final stack and compact stack indices. IsEmpty reports whether any values remain.
constraints: Examples are [operations,arguments]: the first operation constructs the class; each later operation calls that method on the same object. The output has one entry per operation: null for construction/void, a returned value otherwise, or {"error":"code"} for the documented BankError. The judge continues after a method error, so failure must leave state unchanged. A failing-constructor transcript contains only construction because no instance exists afterward. There are 1..2001 operations; integer values and indices fit signed 32 bits.

SetOfStacks(capacity) requires capacity in 1..256; otherwise throw BankError('capacity'). Pop on an empty collection throws BankError('empty'). PopAt with a nonexistent or negative stack index throws BankError('index'), including PopAt(0) on an empty collection.

After each successful operation, all small stacks except possibly the last are full. Rollover preserves the relative order of all values other than the removed value when the small stacks are concatenated bottom-to-top. Failed operations preserve all contents and indices.

examples.explanation: With capacity 2, pushes 1,2,3,4 create [1,2] and [3,4]. PopAt(0) returns 2, moves 3 into the first stack and leaves [1,3] and [4]. Pop then returns 4 and removes the last small stack; the next Pop returns 3.

ctci6_5_1.description: Replace bits low through high, inclusively, of word with insert's bit pattern aligned so its bit zero lands at low. Preserve every bit outside that interval and return the resulting word.
constraints: Inputs and results are signed 32-bit integers. Interpret them as exactly 32 two's-complement bits, numbered 0 (least significant) through 31. Convert the resulting pattern back to its signed 32-bit value. Do not sign-extend into an unbounded Python integer or an extra JavaScript bit.

0 <= low <= high <= 31. The unsigned 32-bit interpretation of insert fits within high-low+1 bits. Negative insert values are therefore valid only for a full-width interval. Inputs satisfy these preconditions; invalid bounds are not a request to return zero.
Do not mutate inputs. The full-width interval [0,31] is valid and returns insert.

examples.explanation: For word 240 (binary 11110000), insert 5 (101), low 1 and high 3, clearing positions 1..3 leaves 11110000. Aligning 101 yields 00001010. OR produces 11111010, or 250. Inserting zero into those positions would clear them rather than preserving old ones.

ctci6_10_7.description: Find ANY absent integer in the full nonnegative signed-32-bit domain 0..2147483647 from a readonly integer file. The provided NumberFile initially points to its first value. ReadNext() returns the next integer, or -1 at end of file. Reset() rewinds to the first value. Implement both memory modes: smallMemory=false permits a one-pass bitmap using up to 1 GiB of auxiliary storage; smallMemory=true permits up to 10 MiB and two passes, and additionally guarantees distinct file values.
constraints: The file contains 0..2147483647 values, each in 0..2147483647, so at least one domain value is absent. Repetitions are allowed only when smallMemory=false. The returned integer must be absent; the smallest absent value is not required.

The callable receives NumberFile, not an array or ranges. Example/test wire storage is an array of inclusive integer ranges [[start,end],...]; the judge lazily streams every value of each range in order, including repeated values from overlapping/repeated ranges in full-memory mode. Each range is nonempty and within the domain. In small-memory mode ranges cannot overlap. The expanded file length obeys the stated bound.

ReadNext has constant cost and returns -1 persistently after EOF until Reset. With full memory, do not Reset and use at most length+1 reads; with small memory, at most one Reset and 2*(length+1) reads. File contents are readonly. Do not inspect private backing storage or retain a file-sized list/set of values; memory budgets concern algorithm storage beyond the supplied stream and language runtime.

A domain bitmap has exactly 2^31 bits = 268435456 bytes and fits the 1 GiB mode. The small-memory mode must avoid that allocation. Its distinct-value promise matters: bucket COUNTS do not prove all values in a bucket are present when duplicates are allowed.

examples.explanation: A file represented by [[0,2],[4,4]] streams 0,1,2,4. Full mode sets those four bits and finds missing 3. In small mode block 0 has count 4<1048576; after Reset, its local bitmap again identifies 3. If [[0,1048575]] is the whole file, block 0 is full, so the small-memory search chooses block 1 and returns 1048576. A file containing 2147483647 must not overflow its stream cursor or last bitmap index.

ctci6_16_8.description: Write a signed 32-bit integer in English words. Use title-case number words, single spaces, no punctuation, no hyphens and no word "and". Prefix a negative number with "Negative "; zero is "Zero". The largest scale needed is Billion.
constraints: value is any signed 32-bit integer, including -2147483648. Return a nonempty string with no leading/trailing spaces. Examples of the exact convention: 21 -> "Twenty One", 105 -> "One Hundred Five", 1001 -> "One Thousand One".

examples.explanation: For -1002003, the low-to-high groups are 3,2,1. They spell Three, Two Thousand and One Million. Reverse the group order and join once to get One Million Two Thousand Three, then prefix Negative. The result is "Negative One Million Two Thousand Three".

constraints: first and second are integers in -10000..10000. operation is exactly subtract, multiply or divide. For divide, second is nonzero. These bounds keep every result in signed 32-bit range and make the repeated-addition baseline runnable.

Do not use subtraction, unary negation of a variable, multiplication, division, remainder, bitwise arithmetic, shifts or helpers that perform those operations (including abs). Increment/decrement by addition is allowed. Preserve caller values.

examples.explanation: For divide(-7,3), obtain magnitude 7 by adding +1 seven times to -7 and accumulating 7. The divisor magnitude is 3 and its additive opposite is -3. Remainders 7->4->1 permit two removals; a third would be negative. The quotient step is -1 because signs differ, so return -2. For multiply(-4,-3), use addend 4 three times, returning 12.

ctci6_16_12.description: Encode an already parsed XML element tree using supplied positive tag/attribute codes. Return an array of string tokens. For each element emit: its decimal name code; each attribute as decimal name code then literal value; "0" ending the attribute list; its nonempty text OR its recursively encoded children in order; and "0" ending the element. The token array preserves complete literal values, including spaces and empty attribute values.
constraints: elementNames, elementTexts and children have equal length n in 0..1000. If n>0, element 0 is the root; children lists form one rooted tree reaching every element exactly once, with valid node indices and specified sibling order. Nonempty elementTexts is allowed only at a leaf. Empty text means no text token; an empty leaf therefore emits its code followed by two end markers. n=0 encodes to [].

attributeOwners, attributeNames and attributeValues have equal length a in 0..1000. Each owner is a valid element index. Emit attributes of an element in their original attribute-array order, even when attributes of different elements are interleaved. An element has no repeated attribute name.

codeNames and codes have equal length 1..9. codeNames are unique ASCII-letter names of length 1..20; codes are distinct integers 1..9. Every element/attribute name appears in this map. Texts and attribute values contain 0..100 ASCII letters/spaces. This literal domain excludes the reserved digit marker; XML parsing, entities, namespaces and mixed text/child content are outside this already-parsed input model.

All arrays, child row objects, values and order are readonly. Return actual literal tokens, not a whitespace-split string: one attribute value containing spaces remains one token. Numeric code tokens use ordinary decimal spelling, and end markers are exactly "0".

examples.explanation: Let element names be [family,person], texts ["",Hello] and children [[1],[]]. Attributes are owners [0,1], names [last,first], values [Tran,Ada]; name codes are family=1, person=2, first=3, last=4. The tokens are ["1","4","Tran","0","2","3","Ada","0","Hello","0","0"]. The last two zeros close person then family; the earlier zeros end their attribute lists.

ctci6_16_13.description: Find a line that divides each of two axis-aligned squares into equal areas. Each row is [left,bottom,side], describing the closed square [left,left+side]×[bottom,bottom+side]. Return [startX,startY,endX,endY], the two outermost boundary intersections of that line across both squares. Either endpoint order is accepted. If the centers coincide, any line through the common center is accepted, with its full outer boundary span.
constraints: squares has exactly two distinct row objects. left and bottom are integers in -1000..1000 and side is an integer in 1..1000. Squares may overlap, touch, contain one another or be identical. Preserve all input objects, rows and values.

ctci6_16_14.description: Find a straight line passing through the largest number of input point occurrences. Return integer coefficients [A,B,C] for A*x+B*y+C=0, with A and B not both zero. Any maximum line is accepted, including equivalent coefficient scaling/sign. Collinearity is exact, with no floating-point epsilon.

Return three signed 32-bit coefficients for a nonempty input. Every nonempty integer-point set has a suitable maximum line with representable integer coefficients. Empty input returns []. For one point or all coincident points, any valid line through that location is accepted; the reference chooses a vertical line.

examples.explanation: For [[0,0],[1,1],[2,2],[0,1]], anchoring at [0,0] groups [1,1] and [2,2] under reduced direction (1,1). That line has three occurrences and equation x-y=0, so [1,-1,0] is valid. Vertical lines use B=0; repeated [0,0] occurrences add to every line through that anchor.

ctci6_17_12.description: Convert a binary search tree of provided BiNode objects IN PLACE into a noncircular, sorted doubly linked list, and return its original first node. Before conversion Node1 is the left child and Node2 the right child. After conversion Node1 must be the previous node and Node2 the next node. constraints: The input is null or the root of one proper binary search tree with 0..1000 nodes. Every node has signed 32-bit Data and no cycles or shared children. Its inorder Data sequence is nondecreasing, so duplicates are allowed; the final list must preserve the original inorder OBJECT order even among equal values.

Return null for an empty tree. Otherwise return the original inorder-first node. Its Node1 must be null; the inorder-last Node2 must be null. Each other previous/next field must identify its actual adjacent original node, and both traversal directions must be consistent. Every input node appears exactly once.

An example/test wire fixture is {nodes:[[data,leftIndex,rightIndex],...],selected:rootIndex}, where -1 denotes null and row position identifies an original object. selected is -1 exactly for no nodes; every row belongs to the selected tree. The callable receives the actual BiNode root, not this fixture. Data is readonly; only Node1/Node2 links may change. C++ callers retain ownership: never delete provided nodes. Auxiliary stacks of original references are allowed.

ctci6_17_26.description: Compute positive Jaccard similarities between distinct documents treated as sets of integer word IDs. Return one row [smallerDocumentId,largerDocumentId,intersectionSize,unionSize] for each pair with a nonempty intersection. The exact similarity is intersectionSize/unionSize; no floating-point rounding is involved. Sort result rows by the two document IDs.
constraints: documentIds has 0..200 distinct signed 32-bit IDs. documents has the same length; each nonnull row contains 0..200 distinct signed 32-bit word IDs. Document/word IDs are identities, not array positions or counts. Preserve both input arrays, every document row and all order/values.

Each returned pair appears once, with IDs in increasing order. Omit disjoint pairs, including pairs of empty documents. Counts are the actual intersection/union sizes, not reduced fraction components. Empty documents have no positive-similarity partner.

examples.explanation: For IDs [10,20,30] and documents [[1,2],[2,3],[]], word 2 links documents 10 and 20 once. Their intersection is 1 and union is 2+2-1=3, so return [[10,20,1,3]], representing exact similarity 1/3. Empty document 30 creates no positive pair.
